title: Word Stress Rules (Nouns/Adjectives vs Verbs/Prepositions)
objectives: Apply 1st-syllable stress default to 2-syllable nouns and adjectives
Apply 2nd-syllable stress default to 2-syllable verbs and prepositions
Use pitch, length, and loudness to signal primary stress

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Word Stress Rules (Nouns/Adjectives vs Verbs/Prepositions)
1. Definition: Two-syllable words follow predictable default stress rules based on part of speech.
2. Rule: Nouns & Adjectives = Stress 1st syllable (TAble, HAPpy, DOCtor, PAper). Verbs & Prepositions = Stress 2nd syllable (reLAX, deCIDE, beTWEEN, beGIN).
3. Why? Germanic root heritage stresses nominal roots, while Germanic prefixes on verbs remain unstressed.
4. How to recognize? Determine word class (noun/adj vs verb/prep) for 2-syllable words.
5. Common examples: TAble, HAPpy, DOCtor, CLEver, MONkey vs reLAX, deCIDE, beTWEEN, aGREE, forGET
6. Counter-examples: Verbs with Germanic prefixes stressing root (un-DO, re-PLAY).
7. Exceptions: Verbs ending in -en, -er, -le stress 1st syllable: LISten, OFfer, ENter, HAPpen, OPen.
8. Common mistakes: Equal stress on both syllables creating unnatural robotic rhythm.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Nouns = FIRST syllable! Verbs = SECOND syllable!
10. Key vocabulary: primary stress, noun stress, verb stress, pitch jump, vowel duration
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟠 B1
13. Associated Visual: ⛰️ High peak on 1st syllable for Nouns, 2nd syllable for Verbs.
14. Key Takeaway: 2-syllable Noun/Adj = 1st! Verb/Prep = 2nd!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Where is stress usually placed in 2-syllable nouns like 'table'? (1st syllable: TAble)
CCQ 2: Where is stress usually placed in 2-syllable verbs like 'decide'? (2nd syllable: deCIDE)
CCQ 3: Where is stress in the verb 'listen'? (Exception: 1st syllable LISten)

elements.content: Identify the stressed syllable based on part of speech:
🎯 Item: happy (adjective) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: HAP-py (1st syllable)
🎯 Item: relax (verb) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: re-LAX (2nd syllable)
🎯 Item: between (preposition) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: be-TWEEN (2nd syllable)
